label: conj:surreal-limit-transfer
title: Surreal limit transfer: limits as standard-part equalities via an $\omega$-evaluation
html:
Conjecture (surreal limit transfer). There is an \omega-evaluation \mathrm{ev}_\omega : \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}} \to \mathbf{No} of real sequences, sending constants to their embedded reals, respecting pointwise addition and multiplication, transferring eventual pointwise domination to the surreal order, and evaluating every convergent sequence infinitesimally close to its limit:

  a_n \to L
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \mathrm{ev}_\omega(a) - L \in \mathfrak{m},
  \qquad
  \mathrm{st}\bigl(\mathrm{ev}_\omega(a)\bigr) = L .

Here \mathfrak{m} is the infinitesimal ideal of the finite valuation ring (valuation ring of finite surreals) and \mathrm{st} the standard-part map.

This is the block-level home for the "move analytic \to surreal" operation: an analytic limit statement becomes a surreal equality up to an infinitesimal — and, after \mathrm{st}, an exact equality. Two consequences are derived, fully proved, from the class fields in the Lean sibling:

  1. Limits are computed by \mathrm{st} \circ \mathrm{ev}_\omega (standardPart_evalOmega_of_tendstoReal).
  2. Limit comparison: if a_n \le b_n eventually and both converge, then \lim a_n \le \lim b_n (tendstoReal_le_of_eventuallyLE) — the eventual inequality is transferred to a single surreal inequality at \omega and the archimedean conclusion recovered by the proved monotonicity of \mathrm{st}. The classical strict-inequality collapse is visible structurally: \mathrm{ev}_\omega(a) < \mathrm{ev}_\omega(b) is compatible with equal standard parts, so only \le survives the wall.

Epistemic status

The conjecture is carried as a content-bearing Lean class with no instance — the honest open state. For the concrete surreals the evaluation exists model-theoretically: Robinson's ultrapower supplies one [robinson1966], and the Berarducci–Mantova identification of surreals with transseries/germs [berarducci-mantova2018] supplies the canonical one for the definable-germ class (evaluation of the germ at \omega). Neither construction is available from the axiomatised SurrealField interface alone, which is exactly why the block is a conjecture rather than a theorem: what is conjectural is the compatibility package on the abstract interface, not the existence of some such map in set theory.

Relation to resummation

For a convergent sequence, \mathrm{st} \circ \mathrm{ev}_\omega is ordinary summation. For a divergent Gevrey-1 asymptotic series the same composite, applied to the Berarducci–Mantova evaluation of the associated transseries, is the median resummation — the identification recorded in st is median resummation. The conjecture is therefore the convergent-sector base case of the resummation dictionary: it fixes the normalisation that any median-resummation extension must restrict to.
